title: Holidays, traditions and celebrations
context:
In this topic you learn vocabulary for holidays and celebrations in Portugal, and you compare them with traditions from your country. The goal is practical: understand the names of important days, say a simple wish, and ask how people celebrate.

- `O 25 de Abril é feriado nacional.` — “25 April is a national holiday.”
- `No Santo António, as pessoas comem sardinhas assadas.` — “On Saint Anthony’s Day, people eat grilled sardines.”
- `No Porto, as pessoas festejam o São João em junho.` — “In Porto, people celebrate Saint John in June.”
- `No Natal, muitas famílias comem bacalhau na consoada.` — “At Christmas, many families eat cod on Christmas Eve.”
- `Boas Festas!` / `Feliz Ano Novo!` — common wishes at the end of the year.
- `Como se festeja o Diwali no teu país?` — “How is Diwali celebrated in your country?”

Watch out:
- `feriado` is a public holiday; it is not the same as any party or festival.
- Contractions are very common: `no Natal`, `no Porto`, `na consoada`, `do 25 de Abril`.

keyItems.support: small basil pot sold at June festivals

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: A public holiday is «um feriado». To say «national holiday», add «nacional».
exercises.sentence: In Portugal, 25 April is a public **holiday**.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: Portuguese uses the single word «Páscoa» for Easter. It is the name of the holiday.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the words in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Ano Novo Chinês» is a fixed name, so learn it as one chunk.
exercises.sentence: Some families celebrate **Chinese New Year** in Portugal.

exercises.prompt: Match each wish with its meaning.
exercises.explanation: These are common ready-made wishes. Learn them as fixed chunks.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two gaps about Portugal.
exercises.explanation: «Feriado» is the noun and «nacional» is the adjective. Together they mean «national holiday».
exercises.template: O 25 de Abril é um ___ ___ em Portugal.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two gaps about Santo António in Lisbon.
exercises.explanation: A very common June tradition is to eat «sardinhas assadas» and buy a «manjerico».
exercises.template: No Santo António muitas pessoas comem ___ assadas e compram ___.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two gaps about Christmas food in Portugal.
exercises.explanation: These two foods are strongly associated with Portuguese Christmas: «bacalhau» for the meal and «bolo-rei» for the season.
exercises.template: No Natal muitas famílias comem ___ na consoada e ___ durante a época festiva.

exercises.prompt: Wish someone a happy new year: «Happy New Year!»
exercises.explanation: This is a fixed wish used at the end of December and on 1 January.

exercises.prompt: Say: «Today is a national holiday in Portugal.»
exercises.explanation: Use «ser» to identify the day: «é feriado nacional».
acceptedAnswers: Em Portugal hoje é feriado nacional.
Hoje é um feriado nacional em Portugal.

exercises.prompt: Say: «On Saint Anthony's Day, people eat grilled sardines.»
exercises.explanation: Use «no» because it is the contraction of «em + o»: «no Santo António».
acceptedAnswers: As pessoas comem sardinhas assadas no Santo António.

exercises.prompt: Say: «At Christmas, many families eat cod at dinner on Christmas Eve.»
exercises.explanation: «Consoada» is the usual Portuguese word for the Christmas Eve dinner.
acceptedAnswers: Muitas famílias comem bacalhau na consoada no Natal.

exercises.prompt: Say: «In Porto, people celebrate São João in June.»
exercises.explanation: For cities, use «em» with contraction where needed: «no Porto».
acceptedAnswers: As pessoas festejam o São João em junho no Porto.

exercises.prompt: A guide says: «Come-se bacalhau na consoada.» Ask, in neutral Portuguese, what people eat at dinner on Christmas Eve.
exercises.explanation: «O que é que...?» is a very common European Portuguese pattern for asking about things.
acceptedAnswers: O que se come na consoada?
O que comem muitas famílias na consoada?
O que é que as pessoas comem na consoada?
O que comem as pessoas na consoada?

exercises.prompt: Your classmate says: «Festeja-se em junho.» Ask when São João is celebrated.
exercises.explanation: To ask about time, use «Quando» or «Em que mês». Both are natural here.
acceptedAnswers: Quando se festeja o São João?
Em que mês é que se festeja o São João?
Em que mês se festeja o São João?

exercises.prompt: Your classmate says: «No meu país, festejamos o Diwali com a família.» Ask your classmate (informal) how Diwali is celebrated in their country.
exercises.explanation: You can learn «Como se festeja ... no teu país?» as a useful ready-made question.
exercises.givenAnswer: No meu país, festejamos o Diwali com a família.
acceptedAnswers: Como é que se festeja o Diwali no teu país?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With «consoada», the phrase is «na consoada» because it is «em + a».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With «tu», regular verbs in the present often end in «-as»: «tu festejas».

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: You can answer with «No meu país...» and say who celebrates with you, what people eat, or what people do.
exercises.question: Como se festeja uma data importante no teu país?
exercises.sampleAnswer: No meu país, festejamos o Eid com a família.

exercises.prompt: Fill the three gaps with a common end-of-year wish.
exercises.explanation: «Feliz Ano Novo!» is a fixed expression, so the three words stay together in this order.
exercises.template: No fim do ano, muitas pessoas dizem: «___ ___ ___!»

exercises.prompt: Your colleague says: «Diz-se “Bom feriado!”.» Ask what people say before a public holiday.
exercises.explanation: Use «O que se diz...?» to ask for the expression people normally use in a situation.
acceptedAnswers: O que é que se diz antes de um feriado?

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Bacalhau» means cod. It is a very common food at Christmas in Portugal.

exercises.prompt: Match each holiday word with its meaning or place.
exercises.explanation: Some items are general words and some are specific Portuguese traditions. Learn them as ready-made cultural words.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "Carnival is in February or March, depending on the year."
exercises.explanation: Carnaval changes date, so in Portugal it can be in February or in March.
exercises.template: O Carnaval é em ___ ou ___, conforme o ano.

exercises.prompt: Say that bolo-rei is a traditional Christmas cake.
exercises.explanation: Use «é» to define something. «De Natal» means it is connected with Christmas.

exercises.prompt: Your classmate answers: «Festeja-se em fevereiro ou março.» Ask when Carnival is celebrated.
exercises.explanation: To ask about time, use «Quando (é que) ...?». Here the verb is impersonal: «se festeja».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The article agrees with the noun after it: «doce» is masculine, so «um doce tradicional», not «uma doce».

exercises.prompt: Say that Sunita celebrates Diwali with friends in Portugal.
exercises.explanation: With a named person, use the 3rd person singular: «festeja». «Com amigos» tells you who she celebrates with.

exercises.prompt: Your friend answers: «Come-se bolo-rei.» Ask what traditional cake people eat at Christmas.
exercises.explanation: Ask about the thing with «Que ...?». «No Natal» is the contraction of «em + o Natal».
acceptedAnswers: Que bolo tradicional é que se come no Natal?
Qual é o bolo tradicional que se come no Natal?

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence about Ramadan and Eid.
exercises.explanation: Eid (Eid al-Fitr) is celebrated at the end of Ramadan, the month of fasting: «Depois do Ramadão, … festejam o Eid».
exercises.template: Depois do ___, muitos muçulmanos festejam o ___ com a família.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: You can answer with a celebration from your country. «Celebra-se» is useful when you talk about what people in general do.
exercises.question: Que festa importante se celebra no teu país?
exercises.sampleAnswer: No meu país, celebra-se o Diwali em família.
